# QA Agent Pipeline — output configuration
#
# Controls where agents write generated artifacts, relative to the project root the
# pipeline is invoked from. Every agent reads this file first (see the "Output Location"
# section at the top of each prompt in prompts/) and falls back to these same defaults
# if this file is missing, so deleting it is safe — it just resets you to defaults.

output_dir: output
runs_subdir: runs
run_id: null   # unset -> agents default to today's date (YYYY-MM-DD); set explicitly (e.g. a
               # release tag or CR number) to keep concurrent cycles cleanly separated

# Optional inputs some agents look for. All may be left null and provided ad hoc by the user
# in conversation instead — these just save asking every time.
inputs:
  requirements_docs: null    # path/glob to SRS/CR doc(s), read by requirements-analyzer
  logs_dir: null              # default directory log-analyzer looks in if none specified
  bug_template: templates/bug-report.template.md

# File/folder names within a run. Rarely need to change these — mainly here so a team can
# rename to match existing conventions without editing every agent prompt. All paths below
# resolve under <output_dir>/<runs_subdir>/<run_id>/ EXCEPT `context`, which lives directly
# under <output_dir>/ — it's refreshed in place across runs, not versioned per cycle.
paths:
  context: context.md
  changes: changes.md
  requirements: requirements.md
  rtm: rtm.md
  rtm_csv: rtm.csv
  code_scan: code-scan.md
  test_plan: test-plan.md
  test_plan_csv: test-plan.csv
  test_cases_dir: test-cases
  test_cases_csv: test-cases.csv
  log_analysis: log-analysis.md
  rca_dir: rca
  bugs_dir: bugs
  test_closure_report: test-closure-report.md
  release_notes: release-notes.md
